title: Tuvan People's Republic
capsule: The Tuvan People's Republic (Тыва Арат Республик) was a Soviet satellite state in the upper Yenisei basin of inner Asia, proclaimed on 14 August 1921 after Bolshevik forces expelled the Chinese administration and a Tannu Tuvan assembly declared independence under Russian auspices. Recognized only by the USSR (1924) and Mongolia (1926), it operated under direct Soviet guidance; Salchak Toka served as the dominant Communist Party secretary from 1932. During World War II the republic contributed its entire gold reserve and roughly 50,000 horses to the Soviet war effort, then on 11 October 1944 its parliament voted for annexation, and the Presidium of the Supreme Soviet incorporated Tuva into the Russian SFSR as an autonomous oblast.
attestation: Boundaries from Seshat Cliopatria (Bennett et al., Scientific Data 2025; CC BY 4.0), digitized from standard historical atlases at ~0.07° resolution. The republic's territory corresponded closely to present-day Republic of Tuva in Russia; its boundaries were defined by the 1914 Russian protectorate arrangements and are reasonably well-attested.
